zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 8, obstructing views from Decks 8, 9, and 10 with diminishing severity as you go higher.
zones.effect: Deck 8 sees boats filling most of the downward view; Deck 9 sees boat tops and partial obstruction; Deck 10 typically clears the boats with horizon intact but boats visible when looking down.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to anyone who values an unobstructed ocean view or dislikes the industrial look of safety equipment; irrelevant to those focused on price, interior cabins, or those who spend little time in the cabin.

zones.what: Deck 6 sits directly above Deck 5 Plaza public areas (shops, atrium activities, guest services) with frequent daytime traffic and announcements.
zones.effect: Potential noise and vibration from foot traffic, announcements, and public gatherings below during the day and evening; quieter overnight.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers or those wanting daytime quiet in the cabin; less relevant to those out exploring the ship most of the day.

zones.what: Lido Deck (14) pool area, Horizon Court buffet, and outdoor activity zones sit directly above mid and aft sections of Decks 11 and 12.
zones.effect: Daytime deck chair scraping, pool activity noise, and buffet traffic overhead from early morning through late evening; Deck 12 closer to the source than Deck 11.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone sensitive to overhead footfall and activity noise, especially morning risers; irrelevant to those joining the Lido action anyway.

zones.what: Princess Theatre (Decks 6-7) sits directly above forward Deck 5 cabins.
zones.effect: Late-night show noise, applause, and foot traffic from theatre audiences overhead until shows end around 10-11pm.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to early sleepers or those turning in before entertainment wraps; non-issue for night owls or those attending the shows.

zones.what: Aft Deck 5 and 6 cabins sit low and near the engine room and propulsion machinery.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and mechanical hum, most noticeable at higher speeds or during maneuvering; felt more than heard.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive sleepers or those who notice and dislike mechanical sensations; often unnoticed by sound sleepers or first-time cruisers.

zones.what: Bow thrusters operate during docking and departure, creating mechanical noise and vibration in forward low-deck cabins.
zones.effect: Short-duration (5-15 minutes) grinding or humming during port arrival and departure; happens early morning in many ports.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers bothered by mechanical noise during port mornings; irrelevant to those already awake or deep sleepers.

zones.what: Grand class has elevator/stair banks forward, midship, and aft on each guest deck, with midship banks seeing the heaviest traffic near main dining rooms and atrium.
zones.effect: Cabins very close to elevator lobbies hear chimes, door mechanisms, and conversation throughout the day and night; midship banks busiest, forward and aft quieter.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to noise-sensitive guests who prefer quiet corridors; appreciated by mobility-limited guests who value proximity over silence.

zones.what: Crew access points and service corridors are typically located forward on guest cabin decks, with most intensive use on lower accommodation decks.
zones.effect: Early morning (5-7am) crew movement for breakfast setup and cabin service staging; brief periods of hallway traffic and door noise.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers in forward cabins near crew access doors; minimal impact on those sleeping through alarms or already early risers.
